draft.title: Causes of water scarcity
card: Water scarcity means there is not enough clean water for people's needs. It can happen even where some water exists, if that water cannot be used.
Natural causes
low or unreliable rainfall, and drought, which is a long period of much less rain than usual.
Human causes
overuse, when people take water faster than it is replaced, and pollution, which makes water unsafe to use.
Access
people may be unable to afford clean water, or live too far from a safe source, such as a village with no pipes or wells.
draft.remember: Scarcity can come from too little rain, too much use, dirty water, or no way to afford or reach clean water.

a.q: A town sits beside a large river, but the river is badly polluted by waste and is unsafe to drink. Which cause of water scarcity does this show?
opts: Pollution making water unsafe to use
Drought causing a long period of low rain
Overuse taking water faster than it refills
Families living too far from any water
a.why: The river holds plenty of water, but pollution makes it unsafe, so people still lack clean water. Drought would mean less rain, and nothing here says rain has fallen short.
a.clue: Is the problem the amount of water or its quality?

b.q: A village in Kenya has a safe, clean borehole, but it is a three-hour walk away. Many families cannot make that trip every day. Why do these families face water scarcity?
opts: They cannot reach clean water
They are in a drought
They have overused the borehole
They have polluted their water
b.why: The water is clean and available, but the families cannot reach it easily, so they are short of usable water. Drought, overuse and pollution are not part of this case, so they do not explain the problem.
b.clue: The water exists and is clean. What stops people using it?

a.best: Pollution making water unsafe to use

problems.detail: The stem says the river is 'badly polluted' and 'unsafe to drink', and the right option repeats those words ('Pollution making water unsafe to use'). A student can match the words without understanding the cause. The stem could describe the situation, such as factory waste and sewage entering the river, without naming pollution or 'unsafe'.
